window.inputs: original requestStart S, requestEnd E, current cursor C; S<=C<=E; actual selector returned segment or nil.
window.A_ge_B: Skip selected segment with unchanged cursor.
window.B_less_than_S: Strict before-request skip; B==S is not this branch.
window.read: [begin,min(B,E)) if positive; equality has no source read. A==E can zero prefix then terminate.
window.advancement: Successful full read advances to min(B,E); zero-length intersection advances at most through prefix. Selector advancement and node lifetime are outside pure planner.
window.source_readiness: Native missing source, zero source length or unready accessor zeros the planned read span. App helper does not invent accessor readiness.

read_contract.retry: Return -2147483645 is retried once only when saved readBegin equals quantized segment start; repeat the read without repeating seek.

read_contract.gain_scope: Gain is passed into native accessor before read; equal-rate explicit app memory backend applies checked gain once after copying. No claim about arbitrary conversion/layout/poststage gain ordering.

defensive_contract.inputs: Finite signed normal-or-zero coordinates, positive normal period yielding positive normal Float32 multiplier; arm64 nearest IEEE with FZ/DN/AH/FIZ off. Signed64 fused result, checked integer differences/sums and request span<=16m. Disjoint input/output structs.
defensive_contract.validation: Upfront finite validation can reject fields that a native early return would not consume. Invalid segments A>=B skip normally; native nonfinite/saturating/wrapping cases reject.
defensive_contract.transactionality: Pure outputs unchanged on validation/range/FP error; no sample buffers are owned or modified.
defensive_contract.application_policy: Caller supplies an explicit rate-derived period and verified constructed descriptors. Synthetic multi-segment windows do not promote arbitrary CPR objects to playable tracks.

candidate.scope: Pure planning, one mapped entry and exact-read status. No provider callback, source samples, accessor allocation/cache or mapper creation is implemented by C helpers.

validation.test_scope: Five numerical reader tests and five direct-memory Swift-stream tests using synthetic media and retained CPR fixtures. No proprietary reader execution.
validation.initial_failure_scope: Swift test-only nested throwing expression syntax; production C/Swift compiled.
validation.release_acceptance: APP014 owns full-suite, GUI and package acceptance; these are not asserted by this native study.

remaining_limits: The actual datum period, provider membership, mapper/loop/locator state and host callbacks remain runtime context, not fabricated constants.
Concrete segment getter pointer/instruction bindings are checked; channel/provider ownership is independently covered by timeline-provider.
The active-project mapping branch was retained but is not reconstructed; one already-mapped entry rounding does not prove identity mapping.
Accessor creation, cache invalidation, layout remapping, asynchronous I/O, outer retry and downstream mixer/plugin/poststage behavior are outside the pure candidate.
App equal-rate immutable-memory copying/gain and worker/device scheduling are application compositions, not Cubase live output comparisons.
Raw-slice Ghidra pseudocode loses imports, types, globals and neighboring calls; original listed bindings supply only bounded context.
Private native image/raw bytes/disassembly remain local research artifacts and are not intended for publication.
